# A waiting run shows its item, its project, who it asks, how many of the quorum answered and the time left to its deadline. The JSON list carries the same data. A finished run keeps its state and loses its wait.
isolate

exec git init -q -b main origin
exec git -C origin add readme.txt
exec git -C origin -c user.name=e2e -c user.email=e2e@example.com commit -q -m start

subst config/projects/local.star

exec obeereal item add local ship-it --title 'Ship it' --body-file body.txt
exec obeereal run ship-it local --workflow flow/ask.star &
waitstatus 'answer by'

# Nobody has answered yet; 48 hours is the deadline, so a little under two days is left.
exec obeereal status
stdout 'item ship-it of local'
stdout 'asks ana, bo, 0 of 2 answered; choices yes, no'
stdout 'answer by [0-9TZ:-]+, 1d23h left'

exec obeereal answer ship-it --as ana yes

# One of the two has answered, so the run still waits.
waitstatus '1 of 2 answered (ana)'

exec obeereal status --json
stdout '"item":"ship-it"'
stdout '"project":"local"'
stdout '"question":"Ship it\?"'
stdout '"quorum":2'
stdout '"heard":\["ana"\]'
stdout '"choices":\["yes","no"\]'
stdout '"time_left_seconds":'

exec obeereal answer ship-it --as bo yes
wait

exec obeereal status
stdout 'done'
! stdout 'answer by'
exec obeereal status --json
stdout '"state":"done"'
! stdout 'time_left_seconds'

-- origin/readme.txt --
The source repository.
-- body.txt --
Ship it.
-- config/projects/local.star --
project(
    source      = "@WORK@/origin",
    base_branch = "main",
    gate        = "true",
    test_report = "r.xml",
)
-- flow/ask.star --
def main(item):
    wait(name = "ask", question = "Ship it?", to = ["ana", "bo"], quorum = 2, choices = ["yes", "no"], timeout = "48h")
